newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FORECAST-Investors to snap up Iberian short bonds.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Investors to snap up Iberian short bonds.

text.p: Bond investors will snap up Portuguese fixed rate Treasury bonds and Spanish Bonos with maturities of up to three years next week, narrowing yield spreads against German Bunds, analysts said.
They said investors expected both Spain and Portugal to pursue significantly more relaxed monetary policies than Germany throughout 1997.
"Spreads of Iberian bonds with maturities of up to three years against Germany could narrow by around 15 basis points next week," said Valentin Fernandez, analyst of Credit Lyonnais in Madrid.

Serge Goncalves of broker FINMAT in London said: "Portugal and Spain will cut rates more aggressively than Germany throughout this year, which is justification for buying bonds with maturities of up to three years."
Analysts said they did not expect demand for five-year Iberian bonds to be as strong next week as it was this week.

Spreads between Bonos with maturities of up to three years and Bunds are between 190 and more than 200 bps. Two-year Portuguese bonds have a spread of about 10 bps above Bonos and three-year Portuguese bonds have a spread of under five bps above Bonos.
"Among shorter bonds, the Portuguese and Spanish paper are expected to show spreads against Bunds of between 150 bp and 180 bps," Goncalves said.

The Bank of Spain yesterday cut its repo rate by 25 bps to 6.0 percent and the Bank of Portugal today kept its absorption rate steady at 6.2 percent and its repo rate unchanged at 6.50 percent. The German repo rate is three percent.
"Even though the Bank of Portugal has kept rates steady today, the market will see that the fundamentals of the economy will require the central bank to cut rates soon," said one bank's analyst.
He added: "I think Portuguese official rates will fall from June and by the end of the year the repo rate could be around five percent."

Henrik Lumholdt, analyst of Bank of America in Madrid, said Mibor futures indicated that the Spanish repo rate would be 5.52 percent in three months, 5.20 percent in six months and 5.00 percent in September.
"I think that at the end of 1997 the Spanish repo could drop to 4.50 percent," he said.
Expectations that year-on-year inflation in Portugal and Spain will drop clearly below three percent in the coming months is reinforcing support for shorter bond prices.
"I think Portuguese and Spanish yield curves will steepen due to strong demand for maturities of up to three years," said Credit Lyonnais's Fernandez.
"But compared with the rest of the curve I consider five year bonds to be a little expensive," he added.
"The spread between maturities of two and five years among Bonos, now 33/34 bps, could increase and exceed 40 bps," Lumholdt said.
Analysts said that, unlike shorter bonds, 10-year yield spreads should stay flat between Portugal and Spain and remain between 90 and 100 bps above Germany.
"With 10-year bonds sensitive to what is happening abroad, I think there will be strong resistance at 90 bps above Bunds," said Fernandez.
